root_idea.summary: A root of strength, overpowering force, and prevailing over another.
root_idea.development: The root develops from exerting force and subduing an opponent to meanings of victory, dominance, defeat, and the resulting state or agent. Related extensions describe predominance, thickness, and dense luxuriant growth.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic plural غُلْبٌ is presented under the supported feminine singular adjective غَلْبَاءُ.

senses.definition: To overcome, defeat, overpower, conquer, or prevail over an opponent or opposing force.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran uses both active and passive forms: the active subject prevails, while the passive subject is overcome or defeated.

senses.definition: To dominate or be overpowered by something; to have something prevail over a person or gain mastery over him.
senses.usage_conditions: With عَلَى, the construction presents the thing or condition that prevails over, or takes control of, someone or something. The Quranic use includes a condition that has overcome its subjects.

senses.definition: One who overcomes or prevails; victorious or dominant.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participle of غَلَبَ, also used substantivally and in the plural for those who prevail or are victorious.

senses.definition: Defeat; the state or result of being overcome.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun used in the Quran in the expression “after their defeat.”

senses.definition: Dense, luxuriant, and large in growth; in the Quran, describing gardens with thick foliage or densely grown trees.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the plural غُلْبٌ, used as an adjective of gardens. The adjective can convey either dense luxuriance or great size in this construction.
A passive participle describing one who has been subjected to another's superior power or force.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take or obtain something from another by superior power or force; to cause someone to lose possession of it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction غَلَبَهُ عَلَيْهِ concerns gaining possession of a thing at another's expense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To force or constrain someone against his will; of an affair, to overwhelm, defeat, or baffle him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a causative or experiential extension of overpowering, including an affair that proves too strong for a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exceed another in a quality or condition, such as surpassing him in fear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The preposition بِـ identifies the quality in which one person exceeds another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a quality to become predominant in a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject may be an abstract quality, such as generosity, that prevails over other qualities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, to resist or refuse having a bridle or leading-rope put upon it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic use describing resistance to being controlled.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be unable to do something, especially to associate with people kindly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the idiom أَيُغْلَبُ أَنْ..., the verb expresses inability rather than victory over an opponent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thick-necked, or thick and short or thick and sloping in the neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person or to a neck; the thickness may result from disease or another cause.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone overcome another, or to secure possession of a town or country by superior force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II is causative and may describe making a person victorious or obtaining territory by force.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be judged to have overcome or surpassed a rival, especially in a poetic contest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This passive Form II construction can report a judgment assigning victory to one contestant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make one word or expression predominate over another in a conventional grammatical usage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical lexicological term for treating one member of a pair or expression as representative of the whole.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vie, contend, or strive with another for victory or superiority.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III describes reciprocal or competitive striving, often followed by an account of who prevailed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To gain mastery over a town or country, or to obtain possession of it by force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V emphasizes attaining control through superior power or force.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To contend with one another for control or possession of a town or country.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VI describes mutual striving or rivalry in taking territory.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For laughter to become vehement in its effect upon a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form X construction describes an overpowering effect, here specifically the force of laughter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of fresh herbage, to mature and become tangled, luxuriant, abundant, or dense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form XII verb describes vegetation attaining full growth and compact density.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act or state of overcoming: victory, conquest, ascendency, mastery, predominance, or superiority.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A frequently used substantive for success in a contest or for obtaining something through superior force.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who overcomes, conquers, or masters others much, often, or quickly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive agent noun that may praise repeated or rapid success.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A designation whose nominal or name-like use has become predominant over another possible sense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical grammatical and lexicological expression, not the ordinary active-participle meaning of غَالِب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The greater part, the majority, or what generally prevails.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In adverbial expressions such as غَالِبًا and فِي الغَالِبِ, it means mostly, generally, or for the most part.

other_classical_meanings.definition: What is most probable or likely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same substantive is used in expressions meaning most probably or in all likelihood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most overpowering, conquering, or mighty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The comparative or superlative adjective can describe a mighty or resistive tribe or overpowering might.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thick-necked; of a neck, thick.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man, a she-camel through its feminine form غَلْبَاءُ, or to a neck.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a mountain or hill, lofty and great.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of the adjective's sense of substantial thickness or magnitude.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation is explained in relation to the lion's thick neck.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where one is overcome or conquered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place noun referring to the location of defeat or subjugation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a poet, overcome repeatedly or judged to have overcome a rival; thus an epithet with contrasting evaluative uses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can describe repeated defeat or, in a contest of poetry, a person judged the victor. The intended sense depends on the construction and convention.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Deprived of something because it has been taken from him by superior force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the passive-participial construction corresponding to غُلِبَ عَلَى الشَّيْءِ, distinct from the general state of being defeated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who overcomes, conquers, subdues, or gains ascendency over another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare intensive or quasi-coordinate derived form functioning as an agent noun.

cautions: The public verb headword is normalized from the internal QAC lemma غَلَبُ to the classical citation form غَلَبَ.
The Quranic adjective group is attested as the plural غُلْبٌ; its supported singular citation form is غَلْبَاءُ.
Lane's citation for the garden expression uses historical Quran-reference notation; the modern example 80:30 is used here because QAC independently supplies and identifies that location.
مُغَلَّبٌ has explicitly attested contrasting evaluations—repeatedly overcome or judged victorious—so both are retained in one Classical Arabic entry.
